title: Counit-normalized transport of adic pullback presentations and completion units
statement:
Let $g:T'\to T$ be a morphism of schemes, with small pro-etale sites and inverse image as in [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]. Let $A,I,P_n=A/I^n,A_T,A_{T'}$ satisfy [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum]. For $W=T,T'$ let $\pi_{W,n}:A_W\to(P_n)_W$ be the projections, and write $q_{W,b,a}:(P_b)_W\to(P_a)_W$ for every quotient map. Let $c_{g,n}:g^{-1}(P_n)_T\xrightarrow{\sim}(P_n)_{T'}$ be the canonical constant-section structure maps, which are isomorphisms by [prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-ring-map]. Suppose two constructions $c_g^{(i)}:g^{-1}A_T\to A_{T'}$, $i=1,2$, have exactly the components
$$\pi_{T',n}c_g^{(i)}=c_{g,n}\,g^{-1}(\pi_{T,n}).$$
Then $c_g^{(1)}=c_g^{(2)}$, and
$$q_{T',b,a}c_{g,b}=c_{g,a}g^{-1}(q_{T,b,a})$$
for all $b\ge a\ge1$. Write $G_i(M)=g^{-1}M\otimes_{g^{-1}A_T,c_g^{(i)}}A_{T'}$ for the resulting module pullback constructions, using sheaf tensor [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. The identity on balanced tensors $x\otimes b\mapsto x\otimes b$ gives a natural isomorphism $\alpha:G_1\xrightarrow{\sim}G_2$.

For $i=1,2$, choose universal total left-derived pairs $(L_i,\varepsilon_i)$ for $Q'G_i$ on the homotopy category of complexes, and $(\widetilde L_i,\widetilde\varepsilon_i)$ for its levelwise strict-tower functor. Here $Q,Q'$ (and $Q_{\operatorname{Tow}},Q'_{\operatorname{Tow}}$) are the source and target localizations [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. The pairs are computed on objectwise K-flat complexes with flat terms using [lem-weil-pbc-diagram-kflat-replacements, lem-pur-left-derived-from-kflat-class]. There are unique natural isomorphisms $e:L_1\to L_2$ and $\widetilde e:\widetilde L_1\to\widetilde L_2$ with
$$\varepsilon_{2,P}e_{QP}=Q'(\alpha_P)\varepsilon_{1,P},\qquad
\widetilde\varepsilon_{2,P_\bullet}\widetilde e_{Q_{\operatorname{Tow}}P_\bullet}=Q'_{\operatorname{Tow}}(\alpha_{P_\bullet})\widetilde\varepsilon_{1,P_\bullet}.$$
These comparisons respect evaluation, constant towers, and the finite-reduction comparisons of [lem-weil-pbc-constant-completion-equivalence], including all quotient transition maps.

For a derived $I$-complete $K$ [def-weil-pbc-intrinsic-completion] let $K_\bullet$ be its strict reduction tower. Set $C_iK=R\lim\widetilde L_iK_\bullet$, with total derived inverse limit as in [prop-weil-pbc-rlim-functoriality]. Define $u_i:L_iK\to C_iK$ by applying $\widetilde L_i$ to the strict quotient augmentation $\Delta P\to(P\otimes_{A_T}(P_n)_T)_n$, $x\mapsto x\otimes1$, and using the constant-tower/derived-limit unit, as in [def-weil-pbc-completed-pullback]. Then $E_K=R\lim(\widetilde e_{K_\bullet}):C_1K\xrightarrow{\sim}C_2K$ is natural and satisfies
$$E_Ku_1=u_2e_K.$$
The constant-tower comparisons used in defining $u_i$ are the ones fixed by the displayed universal counit equations. The finite maps and counits retained by these comparisons determine the same inverse adjoint mates for open extension when applied in a cartesian open square, with extension the sheafified presheaf construction [def-weil-extension-by-zero-presheaf, def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification]. No invertibility of $c_g^{(i)}$ or identification of constant and completed ambient coefficient categories is assumed.

proof.text: By [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum], sections of $A_{T'}$ are compatible families, so its projections are jointly injective on morphisms from any sheaf. The prescribed components therefore give $c_g^{(1)}=c_g^{(2)}=:c_g$. For a quotient homomorphism $q:P_b\to P_a$, the two maps $(P_b)_T\to g_*(P_a)_{T'}$ obtained by first applying $q$ or first sending a constant section to its pullback both send $z\in P_b$ to the constant section $q(z)$. They agree on the defining coefficient presheaf, hence on its sheafification. Taking their adjuncts under the inverse-image adjunction of [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image] gives $q_{T',b,a}c_{g,b}=c_{g,a}g^{-1}(q_{T,b,a})$. Here [prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-ring-map] identifies exactly these constant-section maps with $c_{g,n}$.

proof.text: Since the two coefficient homomorphisms are equal, the balancing relations defining $G_1(M)$ and $G_2(M)$ coincide. Thus $x\otimes b\mapsto x\otimes b$ and the identical reverse formula are well-defined inverse maps on presheaf tensor products [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. They commute with restrictions, with module maps $h$ (both routes send $x\otimes b$ to $g^{-1}h(x)\otimes b$), and degreewise with differentials. Sheafification [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification] gives the natural isomorphism $\alpha$, also on strict diagrams: each transition square is this same naturality square.

proof.text: Use the universal pairs in [lem-pur-left-derived-from-kflat-class]. Composition $Q'\alpha\,\varepsilon_1:L_1Q\to Q'G_2$ induces a unique $e:L_1\to L_2$ with $\varepsilon_2(eQ)=Q'\alpha\,\varepsilon_1$. Applying the same universal property to $\alpha^{-1}$ produces $d:L_2\to L_1$. The composites $de$ and $ed$ have respectively counit composites $\varepsilon_1$ and $\varepsilon_2$, by substitution and $\alpha^{-1}\alpha=1$; uniqueness gives $de=1$, $ed=1$. This proves both invertibility and the asserted normalization. Repeat in the abelian category of strict towers to obtain $\widetilde e$. The resolving classes here exist for the one-object category and the small category $J=\mathbf N_{\ge1}^{\mathrm{op}}$ by [lem-weil-pbc-diagram-kflat-replacements]; its second assertion says that both pullbacks invert the quasi-isomorphisms in those classes. On any such replacement $P$ the counits are invertible and the formula is $e_{QP}=\varepsilon_{2,P}^{-1}Q'(\alpha_P)\varepsilon_{1,P}$, and likewise for $P_\bullet$.

proof.text: Take a strict replacement $P_\bullet\to M_\bullet$ from [lem-weil-pbc-diagram-kflat-replacements]. Evaluation gives K-flat complexes with flat terms. Since evaluation is exact [lem-weil-tower-category-levelwise-abelian], the computations of the preceding step identify both $\operatorname{ev}_n\widetilde L_i(M_\bullet)$ and $L_i(\operatorname{ev}_nM_\bullet)$ with $Q'G_i(P_n)$; the comparison between presentations is $Q'\alpha_{P_n}$ on either route. The constant diagram $\Delta P$ is itself objectwise K-flat with flat terms; hence both $\widetilde L_i\Delta(QP)$ and $\Delta L_i(QP)$ have representative $\Delta G_i(P)$, and their presentation comparison is $\Delta\alpha_P$. These identifications are natural: resolve a chain arrow as a diagram indexed by $J\times[1]$, so its two endpoints and its map are resolved simultaneously. Naturality is then the ordinary naturality of $\alpha$; the objectwise quasi-isomorphisms are inverted by the cited replacement theorem. A roof in the localization is handled by its two chain arrows and inversion of its quasi-isomorphism. Any input has a replacement of this kind, so these computations also fix the comparisons uniquely. The constant-tower identification is the one used in [def-weil-pbc-completed-pullback].

proof.text: For a K-flat flat-term representative $P$ of $K$, put $R_\bullet(P)=(P\otimes_{A_T}(P_n)_T)_n$ with the strict quotient transitions of [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum]. Use the finite-reduction isomorphisms of [lem-weil-pbc-constant-completion-equivalence], which are natural for the projection-induced ring map and commute with quotient transitions. The ring map in both presentations is precisely that map by Step 1. At the ordinary tensor level their scalar comparisons use the same balancing maps: $((x\otimes b)\otimes a)\mapsto x\otimes q_{b,a}(b)a$, with reverse $x\otimes a\mapsto(x\otimes1)\otimes a$. Inserting $\alpha$ before or after either map gives the same displayed tensor. Thus conjugating each finite-reduction comparison by the presentation comparisons leaves it unchanged. To read this calculation in the derived category, resolve the entire strict complex $R_\bullet(P)$ by an objectwise K-flat flat-term diagram, using [lem-weil-pbc-diagram-kflat-replacements], and use the counit computations of Step 3. The quotient complexes $P\otimes(P_n)_T$ need not be K-flat over $A_T$; they are not used as pullback resolutions. Naturality of the cited finite-reduction comparisons and the identity tensor maps proves the same square on these resolved diagrams. The transitions are already arrows of those diagrams, and both routes send a tensor to its image under the same $q_{b,a}$. Consequently the comparisons respect every quotient map in the strict tower, rather than only its separate derived evaluations.

proof.text:
Let $a_P:\Delta P\to R_\bullet(P)$ be the augmentation, $a_{P,n}(x)=x\otimes1$. It is strict: $(1\otimes q_{b,a})(x\otimes1)=x\otimes1$, and it commutes with differentials and with maps of $P$. This is the augmentation in [def-weil-pbc-completed-pullback]. Write $b_{i,K}:\Delta L_iK\xrightarrow{\sim}\widetilde L_i\Delta K$ for the normalized constant-tower comparison of Step 4, and set $v_i=\widetilde L_i(Q_{\operatorname{Tow}}a_P)b_{i,K}$. Naturality of the actual transformation $\widetilde e$ at the derived morphism $Q_{\operatorname{Tow}}a_P$ gives
$$\widetilde e_{K_\bullet}v_1=v_2\Delta(e_K).$$
Indeed Step 4 gives $\widetilde e_{\Delta K}b_{1,K}=b_{2,K}\Delta(e_K)$, and substitution into the naturality equation gives the displayed formula. This is an equality in the derived category of strict towers; no lift of $a_P$ into an independently chosen target resolution is being assumed.

proof.text: The functor $R\lim$ of [prop-weil-pbc-rlim-functoriality] sends $\widetilde e_{K_\bullet}$ and its inverse to mutually inverse arrows. Thus $E_K=R\lim(\widetilde e_{K_\bullet})$ is an isomorphism. Its naturality follows by applying this same functor to the naturality square of $\widetilde e$ composed with the strict reduction functor $K\mapsto K_\bullet$ of [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum]. Applying it to the equality of Step 6 gives $E_KR\lim(v_1)=R\lim(v_2)R\lim\Delta(e_K)$.

proof.text:
Write $\eta_C:C\to R\lim\Delta C$ for the constant-tower unit constructed in [def-weil-pbc-completed-pullback]. It is natural in $C$: for a chain map $h:C\to D$, choose the functorial tower K-injective resolution used in [prop-weil-pbc-rlim-functoriality]. Its map $I(\Delta h)$ sends each component of $\Delta C\to I(\Delta C)$ to the corresponding component of $\Delta D\to I(\Delta D)$ composed with $h$. Factoring the compatible families through the ordinary inverse limit therefore gives $(R\lim\Delta h)\eta_C=\eta_Dh$. The same equality holds for inverses of quasi-isomorphisms, hence for derived arrows. In particular $(R\lim\Delta e_K)\eta_{L_1K}=\eta_{L_2K}e_K$. By definition $u_i=R\lim(v_i)\eta_{L_iK}$; substitution into the last equation of Step 7 now gives
$$E_Ku_1=R\lim(v_2)R\lim\Delta(e_K)\eta_{L_1K}=R\lim(v_2)\eta_{L_2K}e_K=u_2e_K.$$
This uses the specified quotient augmentation and its constant-tower normalization throughout.

proof.text: For the final clause, in a cartesian open square identify the open sites with slice sites using [lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization]. This identification also restricts the completed coefficient sheaves: on an object over the open, their sections are the same compatible families of finite coefficient sections. Apply [lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact] to these ringed slice sites. Its extension is exactly $j_!F=P_F^\#$ with $P_F$ from [def-weil-extension-by-zero-presheaf]. The adjunction counit $j_!j^*H\to H$ sends the generator $s$ in the summand indexed by $\varphi:V\to U$ to the same section $s\in H(V)$. The unit sends $s$ on $V\to U$ to its generator in that summand. These descriptions follow by applying the adjunction's presheaf-to-sheaf factorization [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification]. Since $\alpha$ is identity on balanced tensors, these unit and counit formulas coincide for the two presentations, also after a finite quotient. The localized pullback comparison is that of [lem-weil-pbc-localize-ringed-site-morphism], induced by restriction of the same ring map $c_g$. Thus its finite maps coincide under Steps 1--5 as well.

source.place: Tags 03DI and 03DJ, lemma-extension-by-zero and lemma-extension-by-zero-exact; generator descriptions in the proof of 03DI

proof.text:
Finally use the explicit inverse adjoint correspondence of [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate]. For $\beta:GR_1\to R_2H$ its inverse mate is
$$L_2G\xrightarrow{L_2G\eta_1}L_2GR_1L_1\xrightarrow{L_2\beta L_1}L_2R_2HL_1\xrightarrow{\varepsilon_2HL_1}HL_1.$$
In the open square take $L_1=j_!$, $R_1=j^*$, $L_2=j'_!$, $R_2=j'^*$ and the finite pullbacks as $G,H$. The two presentations give the same $\beta$ by the localized comparison in Step 9; that step also gives the same $\eta_1,\varepsilon_2$. Substitution into the displayed three-factor composite proves equality of the inverse mates. This is equality of the finite sheaf maps and counits themselves, and the computations in Steps 3--5 carry their normalized derived comparisons with them. It neither asserts that taking mates preserves arbitrary isomorphisms nor requires an inverse to the completed coefficient map. In particular all arguments remain in the distinct ambient coefficient categories specified in the statement.

split_report.summary: Proved coefficient-map uniqueness, quotient naturality, the balanced tensor isomorphism, both counit-normalized universal comparisons, strict evaluation/constant/finite-reduction compatibility, and the completion-unit square. Kept the quotient tower distinct from its K-flat replacement and checked open inverse mates by the presheaf generator and adjunction formulas. Reused existing nodes throughout; no statement change or new node.

Mathematics: the component hypothesis plus the limit-sheaf definition in the adic datum force c^(1)=c^(2) (Step 1). The quotient square holds because the adjuncts g_*(q)rho_b and rho_a q agree on constant sections and hence after sheafification. So G_1=G_2 and alpha is the identity (Step 2). I checked both hypotheses of lem-pur-left-derived-from-kflat-class through lem-weil-pbc-diagram-kflat-replacements, for J the singleton, N^op and Jx[1] (Steps 3-4). Exactness of Q'G_i on the homotopy category is one line. Step 5 resolves the quotient tower again instead of treating it as K-flat, which is correct. I recomputed e~ v_1 = v_2 Delta(e) (Step 6), E_K u_1 = u_2 e_K through naturality of eta for the functorial K-injective model (Steps 7-8), and the inverse-mate substitution (Steps 9-10). Steps 6-8 agree with the augmentation and unit construction in def-weil-pbc-completed-pullback. Non-load-bearing remarks: Step 9's generator formulas for unit and counit come from the 03DI construction, but Step 10 needs only that both presentations use the same adjunction. The report mislabels 05S9 and lists a citations.json that is not in the commit. Edge cases tested: empty T', g=id, a=b, unit ideal, U=X, K=0. No fixes made.
